# Risk Review and Escalation Protocol Checklist

## Purpose
This checklist provides a structured approach for reviewing, assessing, and escalating project risks. Use this template regularly throughout the project lifecycle to ensure risks are proactively managed and appropriately escalated.

## Risk Identification
- [ ] Review risk register for new or changed risks
- [ ] Solicit risk inputs from all team members
- [ ] Review previous retrospective action items for risk themes
- [ ] Analyze project dependencies for potential risks
- [ ] Review external factors (market, regulatory, organizational changes)
- [ ] Consider technical risks (architecture, scalability, security)
- [ ] Assess resource and capacity risks
- [ ] Evaluate schedule and timeline risks

## Risk Assessment
- [ ] Document risk description clearly and specifically
- [ ] Assign risk impact level (High/Medium/Low)
  - High: Major impact on project success, schedule, or quality
  - Medium: Moderate impact, workarounds may be needed
  - Low: Minor impact, manageable within team
- [ ] Assign risk likelihood/probability (High/Medium/Low)
  - High: Likely to occur (>50% probability)
  - Medium: Possible occurrence (20-50% probability)
  - Low: Unlikely but possible (<20% probability)
- [ ] Calculate risk priority (Impact × Likelihood)
- [ ] Identify risk category (technical, schedule, resource, dependency, etc.)
- [ ] Determine risk owner responsible for monitoring and mitigation

## Risk Mitigation Planning
- [ ] Define mitigation strategy for each risk
  - Avoid: Change plan to eliminate risk
  - Mitigate: Take actions to reduce probability or impact
  - Transfer: Shift responsibility to another party
  - Accept: Acknowledge and monitor without active mitigation
- [ ] Document specific mitigation actions with owners and due dates
- [ ] Identify triggers or indicators for risk escalation
- [ ] Define contingency plans for high-priority risks
- [ ] Estimate resources needed for mitigation activities
- [ ] Set risk review frequency based on priority

## Escalation Criteria
- [ ] Risk remains High/High (high impact, high likelihood) for 2+ weeks
- [ ] Risk impact threatens project timeline by >2 weeks
- [ ] Risk impact threatens project budget by >10%
- [ ] Risk threatens critical path or key dependencies
- [ ] Risk requires additional resources beyond team capacity
- [ ] Risk involves cross-team or organizational dependencies
- [ ] Risk has potential legal, security, or compliance implications
- [ ] Mitigation efforts have not reduced risk level

## Level 1 Escalation (Team Level)
- [ ] Risk discussed in daily standup or team meeting
- [ ] Team members collaborate on mitigation approach
- [ ] Project Manager documents risk in risk register
- [ ] Mitigation actions assigned to team members
- [ ] Risk monitored at team level for 1-2 weeks
- [ ] Progress on mitigation tracked in team status updates

## Level 2 Escalation (Product Management)
When risk meets escalation criteria:
- [ ] Project Manager prepares risk escalation summary
  - Risk description and current status
  - Impact on project goals, timeline, and resources
  - Mitigation efforts attempted
  - Recommended actions and required support
- [ ] Risk escalated to Product Manager/Product Lead
- [ ] PM and PdM review risk and mitigation options
- [ ] Additional resources or authority provided if needed
- [ ] Escalation outcome documented in risk register
- [ ] Stakeholder communication prepared if needed
- [ ] Follow-up review scheduled within 1 week

## Level 3 Escalation (Executive/Sponsor)
When risk remains unresolved or has severe impact:
- [ ] Product Lead prepares executive summary
  - Business impact and strategic implications
  - Options analysis with trade-offs
  - Resource requirements or policy changes needed
  - Recommended decision and rationale
- [ ] Risk escalated to project sponsor or executive leadership
- [ ] Executive decision meeting scheduled promptly
- [ ] Decision documented with clear action plan
- [ ] Organizational communication coordinated
- [ ] Project plan updated based on decision

## Cross-Team Escalation
For risks involving dependencies on other teams:
- [ ] Dependency risk documented with specific details
- [ ] Dependent team's Project Manager notified
- [ ] Joint risk review meeting scheduled
- [ ] Mutual mitigation plan developed
- [ ] Shared accountability defined
- [ ] Regular cross-team sync scheduled for monitoring
- [ ] Escalation to shared leadership if needed

## Risk Communication
- [ ] Risk register updated with current status
- [ ] High-priority risks included in weekly status updates
- [ ] Stakeholders notified of risks that may impact them
- [ ] Team informed of escalation outcomes and actions
- [ ] Communication tailored to audience (technical vs. business)
- [ ] Transparent about risk status without creating alarm

## Regular Risk Review Cadence
- [ ] Weekly risk review in team sync or standup
- [ ] Monthly comprehensive risk register review with stakeholders
- [ ] Sprint retrospectives include risk identification
- [ ] Milestone reviews assess risk management effectiveness
- [ ] Risk trends analyzed and reported to leadership

## Risk Closure
- [ ] Risk mitigation completed and verified
- [ ] Risk likelihood or impact reduced below threshold
- [ ] Risk no longer relevant to project
- [ ] Lessons learned captured for future projects
- [ ] Risk status updated to "Closed" in register
- [ ] Team notified of risk closure

## Documentation
- [ ] All risks documented in centralized risk register
- [ ] Risk register includes: ID, description, impact, likelihood, owner, status, mitigation plan
- [ ] Escalation history tracked for each risk
- [ ] Risk review meeting notes documented
- [ ] Lessons learned captured at project closure

## Success Criteria
Risk management is effective when:
- Risks are identified early and proactively managed
- Escalation occurs promptly when criteria are met
- Mitigation actions reduce risk levels effectively
- No major surprises impact project success
- Team demonstrates risk awareness and ownership
- Stakeholders are appropriately informed of risks
